question: Assume today is 2026-08-25. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births in Japan in July 2026, as first reported in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (which also count foreign nationals in Japan).

target.what: Number of live births occurring in Japan during July 2026, as counted in the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's preliminary monthly vital statistics (人口動態統計速報), which includes foreign nationals residing in Japan
target.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW), Japan
target.cadence: monthly preliminary release, typically published roughly two months after the reference month (e.g., July data released around early September)
target.caveats: The preliminary monthly vital statistics (速報) counts births by date of occurrence registered in Japan, including foreign nationals; it differs from the annual confirmed 確定 figures and from the Japanese-nationals-only 概数. As of the 2026-08-25 cutoff, July 2026 preliminary figures would not yet be pub

Failure mode: a July seasonal share far from average or a 2026 annual level materially different from 705,809. a3.role: July 2026 vs July 2025 year-on-year change factor

methods.rationale: Same-month year-on-year route: the July 2025 level is reconstructed as the 2025 annual preliminary total times a July seasonal share (a4), then carried to July 2026 by a near-flat year-on-year factor (a3) justified by the +0.4% Jan–May 2026 cumulative and −0.4% trailing-12-month change. Shared dependency with m2 on p26; the main failure mode is a July seasonal share far from 1/12. The unit is person because the share and change factor are dimensionless.

assumptions.name: July 2026 level relative to May 2026 preliminary monthly births
assumptions.rationale: July and May monthly birth counts in Japan are typically within a few percent of each other; the Jan–May 2026 cumulative is +0.4% year-on-year (p43 vs p44) and the trailing 12 months are −0.4% (p45 vs p46), so the mid-2026 monthly flow is near-flat. A factor centred at 1.0 with a ±7% 10–90 range covers normal month-to-month variation and the recent softening.
assumptions.applies_when: The May 2026 preliminary level is a valid proxy for the July 2026 monthly flow, i.e. no large July-specific shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large July-specific birth surge or collapse, or a strong seasonal July-vs-May gap in preliminary monthly data.

assumptions.name: July share of annual all-nationality births
assumptions.rationale: July is a near-average month; 1/12 ≈ 0.0833. Japanese monthly birth shares vary only modestly around the mean, so a share near 0.083 with a ±6% relative range is appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 annual level is close to the 2025 preliminary level and July's seasonal share is near average.
assumptions.falsified_by: Historical monthly shares showing July systematically far from 1/12, or a 2026 annual level far from 705,809.

assumptions.name: July 2026 vs July 2025 year-on-year change factor

assumptions.applies_when: The flat 2026 year-on-year trend continues into July.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that July 2026 diverges sharply from the Jan–May 2026 flat trend.

assumptions.name: July 2025 preliminary all-nationality births as a fraction of the 2025 annual preliminary total

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
